language.description: The language from which this code model was parsed or target language for which it was generated.

title:
A "code model" represents a set of classes and global code that can be translated to code in various languages.
This is the "uber abstract syntax tree (AST)" on which code processing tools can operate without being
language-specific.

It aligns similar features across languages, but will include elements that are not present in every language.
For example, every language supports function calls, but only Python supports calls with "keyword arguments."
Keyword arguments are represented in the code model, but valid Java and JavaScript method calls require them to
be replaced with positional arguments.

There are a set of fundamental "leaf nodes", such as {@link Code.BinaryOp}. These are the read-only generic nodes
that aren't necessarily legal in all (or potentially any) language. For example, the binary operator `@` (matmul)
is only supported by Python.

One step more specific are the "language nodes", such as {@link Code.Java.BinaryOp}. This is the Java-specific
implementation of binary operation and actually knows how to write them. In addition to writing, these nodes may
have custom validation.

Since authoring follows the builder pattern, each leaf node also has a corresponding authoring node. For example,
{@link Code.Authoring.BinaryOp}. Authoring nodes with complex sub-structure may add convenience methods for creating
it. See {@link Code.Authoring.DefinedClass} for example. Authoring nodes are mutable.

| Leaf Node | Authoring Node     | Language Node |
|-----------|--------------------|---------------|
| Method    | Authoring.Method   | Java.Method   |
| BinaryOp  | Authoring.BinaryOp | Py.BinaryOp   |

To avoid a lot of manual work in validation, wherever possible nodes in the AST are annotated with the language
support (including version if necessary) using the {@link Ann.Code @code} annotation. For example, in
{@link Code.BinaryOperator}, `@` operator is marked as being unsupported in Java and JavaScript:
```type
@code(java="none", js="none")
MATMUL = '@'
```

@see Code.Authoring
@see Code.Lang
@see Ann.Code
